section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses a study on body size ratings among young Black women. It highlights that participants selected a smaller personal ideal body size compared to their perceived ethnic group ideal, potentially due to weight-related stigmatization and media influence. The analyses also indicated that participants perceived their actual body size to be smaller than a typical ethnic female peer, despite a significant portion of the sample being overweight or obese. The section explores theoretical perspectives related to these findings.
